source.citation: Journal article Expression of the cultural identities of the Cameroonian people: diversity of dress (1961 to 2020), in Échanges, via AJOL. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.cultural_areas: Traditional dress is usually described by four cultural areas: Fang-Beti-Bulu, Sawa, Grassfields and Soudano-Sahelian.
attributes.regional_outfits: Ndop (Bamileke), tiè-yàa (Bamoun), toghu (Northwest) and kaba ngondo (Littoral).
attributes.spread: Outfits once tied to specific peoples have spread nationwide. Batik, formerly the ritual dress of the Bamileke, Bamoun and Bamenda peoples in the west, is now worn by all Cameroonians and in the diaspora. The kaba ngondo, from the Littoral, has become a national outfit.
attributes.wax_and_pagne: Loincloth fabrics (bazin, wax, serrated) have origins in the Far North, after woven fabrics (leppi). Wax is the most widely used.

source.citation: Journal article on dress in Cameroon (AJOL), a KNUST report on the 2025 Akwaaba Night Cameroon fashion parade, and the Ultimate Traditional Designs page on the Toghu. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.origin: Bamenda and the grassfields of the Northwest Region.
attributes.description: An embroidered velvet outfit, often a sleeveless vest.
attributes.past_use: Once reserved for royalty and dignitaries.
attributes.now: Widely worn at ceremonies and by Cameroonians abroad.

source.citation: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Royal display cloth (ndop), the Saint Louis Art Museum, the University of Michigan Museum of Art, and The Common. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.origin: Grassfields and the Bamileke Plateau of western Cameroon.
attributes.making: Handwoven cloth that is dyed with resist techniques, often in indigo blue.
attributes.use: A royal display cloth that sets the scene at royal ceremonies and festivals, a funerary cloth, and a favourite gift between leaders and elites.
attributes.history: The patterns are said to follow cloth from eastern and central Nigeria brought by Hausa traders.
attributes.meaning: Symbolises wealth, power and royal privilege.

source.citation: Journal article on dress in Cameroon (AJOL), and a KNUST report on the 2025 Akwaaba Night Cameroon fashion parade. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.origin: The Littoral Region, among the Duala (Sawa).
attributes.occasions: Often worn during the annual Ngondo festival.
attributes.now: Has become a national outfit worn in many places and circumstances.

source.citation: Journal article on dress in Cameroon (AJOL). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: Printed cloth worn as wrappers (pagnes) and tailored outfits.
attributes.origin_note: The variants of the loincloth (bazin, wax, serrated) have origins in the Far North.
